title: How to prevent AI from harming mathematics

• WORLD VIEW

Mathematicians must urgently recognize AI’s impacts on their field — and act swiftly to mitigate threats.

By

  1. Jim Portegies

    1. Jim Portegies is a mathematician working on artificial intelligence at Eindhoven University of Technology, Eindhoven, the Netherlands.

Science as we know it is under threat from rapid developments in artificial intelligence. Generative AI is fuelling a rise in submissions of low-quality research papers written with the help of chatbots. And technology companies control the most powerful models. With investments in AI for science accelerating, it might not be long until tech firms effectively shape the questions that researchers ask.

Why mathematics is set to be revolutionized by AI

Mathematics is particularly affected, because the discipline lies at the heart of AI systems. The work of many maths researchers also spills into ethical territory. AI models can be used for warfare or mass surveillance and to fuel political disturbances. AI use also affects the environment through the systems’ demand for energy and water.

This is why, with 15 colleagues, I wrote the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics. It calls on all mathematicians — as individuals and as a community — to ensure that the integration of AI into the field brings benefits, not irrevocable harm. AI should speed up processes or help researchers to gain insights; it should not erase expertise, create rifts in the community or weaken the educational system. The declaration was published on 2 June. Since then, it has been signed by roughly 3,000 scientists, most of whom are research mathematicians, and attracted interest from mathematical organizations and the press.

Even so, I think many community members do not grasp the urgency. Mathematician Terence Tao, who received the 2006 Fields Medal, stated in his endorsement of the declaration that the community should have started discussing AI’s implications years ago. Others agree.

The declaration is the result of a September 2025 workshop in Leiden, the Netherlands, that brought together around 60 mathematicians, computer scientists, historians, philosophers and social scientists to discuss the mechanization of mathematical research.

All participants agreed that action is needed urgently, despite having a range of views and predictions about what AI might mean for the discipline. I was part of a representative group of 16 delegates who worked on charting a course for the field.

How AI is reshaping discovery in maths and physics

The declaration identifies core values of mathematics: transparency, scientific integrity and proper attribution of previous work by situating new research in existing literature. It sets out merit-based standards: the ability to learn and work in mathematics on the basis of skills, rather than any form of privilege. And it emphasizes autonomy: as a community, mathematicians should have a large say in the field’s direction.

The document calls on mathematicians to ensure that their work is correct, adhere to open science and provide enough information so that manuscripts can be reviewed thoroughly. They should insist on human authorship and disclose AI use. And they should make informed ethical decisions regarding which tools to use and whether to collaborate with industry.

• 世界观
  • 27 July 2026

数学家必须紧急认识到人工智能对其领域的影响，并迅速采取行动减轻威胁。

By

  1. Jim Portegies Jim Portegies 是荷兰埃因霍温埃因霍温科技大学从事人工智能研究的数学家。

我们所知的科学正受到人工智能快速发展的威胁。 生成式人工智能正在推动在聊天机器人的帮助下提交的低质量研究论文的增加。 科技公司控制着最强大的模型。 随着科学领域人工智能投资的加速，科技公司可能用不了多久就能有效地解决研究人员提出的问题。

为什么人工智能将彻底改变数学

数学尤其受到影响，因为该学科是人工智能系统的核心。 许多数学研究人员的工作也涉及伦理领域。 人工智能模型可用于战争或大规模监视，并助长政治骚乱。 人工智能的使用还通过系统对能源和水的需求影响环境。

这就是为什么我与 15 位同事共同撰写了《人工智能和数学莱顿宣言》。 它呼吁所有数学家——作为个人和社区——确保人工智能融入该领域带来好处，而不是不可挽回的伤害。 人工智能应该加快流程或帮助研究人员获得见解；它不应抹杀专业知识、在社区中制造裂痕或削弱教育体系。 该声明于 6 月 2 日发布。 从那时起，大约有 3,000 名科学家签署了该协议，其中大多数是研究数学家，并引起了数学组织和媒体的兴趣。

即便如此，我认为许多社区成员并没有意识到紧迫性。 获得 2006 年菲尔兹奖的数学家陶哲轩在支持该宣言时表示，社区早在几年前就应该开始讨论人工智能的影响。 其他人也同意。

该宣言是 2025 年 9 月在荷兰莱顿举行的研讨会的结果，该研讨会汇集了约 60 名数学家、计算机科学家、历史学家、哲学家和社会科学家，讨论数学研究的机械化。

所有参与者都同意，尽管对于人工智能对该学科的意义有一系列的看法和预测，但仍需要立即采取行动。 我是由 16 名代表组成的代表小组的一员，他们致力于为该领域制定路线。

人工智能如何重塑数学和物理学的发现

该宣言确定了数学的核心价值：透明度、科学完整性以及通过将新研究置于现有文献中对先前工作的正确归属。 它规定了基于成绩的标准：基于技能而不是任何形式的特权来学习和工作数学的能力。 它强调自主性：作为一个社区，数学家应该对该领域的方向有很大的发言权。

该文件呼吁数学家确保他们的工作正确，坚持开放科学并提供足够的信息，以便手稿能够得到彻底审查。 他们应该坚持人类作者身份并公开人工智能的使用。 他们应该就使用哪些工具以及是否与行业合作做出明智的道德决策。
